cards.text: This is a psalm of Asaph, chief of the worship leaders King David appointed (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). It opens with God presiding in the divine assembly. Friend, the most serious meeting in my bakery is me versus me deciding chocolate chips or sprinkles, but THIS is a meeting.

cards.question: God presides in the divine assembly. He isn't just sitting in. He's there as the ___

cards.text: Then God speaks, and He opens with a question. You ever get called into a meeting and the boss starts with "How long are we gonna keep doing this?" NOBODY in that room is relaxed.

cards.question: In the divine assembly, God asks how long they'll keep doing something. What is it?

answers.text: Judging unjustly and favoring the wicked
Ignoring the feasts and the sacrifices
Refusing to hear any cases at all

cards.text: So what SHOULD they be doing? God LAYS. IT. OUT, and He's just getting started.

cards.question: God tells the assembly whose cause to defend. Whose is it?
God also tells the assembly to uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed, and to rescue the weak and needy from the hand of the wicked.

cards.text: Then comes a heavy line. They don't know, they don't understand, and they wander in the darkness. You ever walk into the kitchen at night with the lights off, bump into EVERYTHING, and then forget why you came in? Same idea, way bigger room.

cards.question: Right after the judges in God's assembly wander in the darkness, what does the psalm say about the foundations of the earth?

cards.text: Now God reminds them of something He has said about them. Friend, when the One who made everything quotes Himself, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: God reminds the ones He's judging what He has said they are. What is it?

answers.text: Gods and sons of the Most High
Priests and servants of the temple

cards.text: Then comes one little word: But. You ever hear "You're doing great, but"? Friend, everything before that but just packed up and left the building.

cards.question: God called them gods and sons of the Most High. What does He say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will be scattered among the nations
They will be turned into servants

cards.question: Besides dying like mortals, God tells the ones He called sons of the Most High that like rulers they will fall.

cards.text: Then the psalm turns. It stops reporting on the assembly and calls out to God Himself to arise.

cards.question: The psalm asks God to arise and judge only the nation of Israel.
The psalm calls on God to judge the earth. What reason does it give?

answers.text: All the nations are His inheritance
The rulers have all stepped down
The nations have asked Him to
